sample_tweets.text: 🚨 🇹🇷 Turkish SMS Service Provider Database Allegedly Offered for Sale  An underground forum user operating under the alias "cardyshop" is advertising what is claimed to be the database of a Turkish company providing SMS, school management, and software services.  - The seller claims the database is being offered as a one-time sale and exceeds 70 GB in size. - According to the advertisement, the dataset contains more than 20,000 unique email addresses and over 1 million unique phone numbers. - Sample records indicate the alleged exposure of customer account information, contact details, company profiles, API credentials, SMS platform configurations, and school management data. - The exposed schema reportedly includes usernames, passwords, API usernames and passwords, API tokens, WhatsApp API keys, company identifiers, tax and billing information, SMS credits, IP addresses, device identifiers, and various account configuration settings.  The forum post includes a partial database schema and claims to offer the complete production database of the platform. While the authenticity of the dataset and the identity of the affected organization could not be independently verified, the advertised content suggests that, if genuine, the database may contain sensitive customer information alongside operational and administrative records related to the SMS platform.  #DataBreach #Turkey #SMS #SchoolManagement #CyberSecurity #ThreatIntelligence #UndergroundForum #DataLeak

🚨 ZoomInfo B2B Data Listing Allegedly Exposes 185M Records  A darkweb forum post claims to offer a dataset containing 185 million business-to-business (B2B) records allegedly sourced from ZoomInfo. The listing, posted on an underground marketplace, asserts that the data was compiled from publicly available indexes and includes sensitive professional and personal information for individuals across the United States.  According to the post, the dataset includes the following fields:  *   First and last names *   Business and personal email addresses *   Job titles, seniority levels, and departments *   Mobile phone numbers and LinkedIn URLs *   Company names, domains, phone numbers, and addresses *   Primary industry classifications and SIC codes *   Estimated company revenue and employee counts  The actor alleges that many of the emails in the dump had not been previously leaked and that the data covers various industries. The post states that the data is being sold for Monero (XMR) only and provides a link to a file hosted on biteblob.com.  ZoomInfo is a major provider of business intelligence data, widely used by sales and marketing teams for lead generation. A breach of this scale could significantly impact privacy and enable targeted phishing or social engineering campaigns against corporate professionals. The threat actor behind the post has a history of distributing large volumes of credentials and stealer logs on forums such as XForums.st, often under aliases like 'Evil_Zone'.  At the time of reporting, ZoomInfo has not commented on the incident, and the authenticity of the 185 million record claim has not been independently verified.

The listing, posted on an underground forum by a user identified as 'feijo', claims to include sensitive customer information such as full names, email addresses, phone numbers, and physical addresses.  According to the post, the dataset includes the following fields:  *   user_id *   full_name *   email *   phone *   phone_verified *   auth_provider *   address *   city *   district *   postal_code *   signup_date *   last_order_date *   orders *   cancelled_orders *   total_spent_krw *   favorite_cuisine *   baemin_club_status *   baemin_club_since *   account_status *   device_model *   os_version *   app_version *   updated_at  Baemin is one of the largest food delivery services in South Korea, operating under Coupang, a major e-commerce conglomerate. The exposure of such a large volume of user data, including precise location information and spending habits, could facilitate targeted phishing campaigns, identity theft, and physical stalking if the leak is authentic.  The threat actor 'feijo' has a history of selling stolen credentials and stealer logs on underground forums like XForums.st. Previous activity includes listings for "Fresh Private HQ ULP LOGS" and Twitter combo lists, suggesting a focus on harvesting and monetizing compromised account data rather than large-scale infrastructure breaches. sample_tweets.text: More to come…  🇰🇵 Security Researcher Infiltrates North Korean Hackers, Uncovers Global Scale of Compromises  A cybersecurity researcher who spent nearly two years inside infrastructure used by North Korean threat actors has revealed evidence of an extensive global intrusion campaign affecting organizations across dozens of countries.  * Researcher Vangelis Stykas says he gained access to North Korean command-and-control systems and analyzed approximately 5 TB of operational data over a 22-month period. * The investigation identified evidence that **1,640 organizations across 57 countries** had been compromised. * Around **700–800 organizations** reportedly suffered severe intrusions, including root access to servers, cloud environments, and cryptocurrency wallets. * Many victims were compromised through the **Contagious Interview** campaign, in which software developers were lured with fake job offers that delivered malware. * The findings will be presented at Black Hat USA, highlighting the scale and persistence of North Korea's cyber operations.   The report illustrates how compromising individual developers and contractors can create a gateway into hundreds of enterprises. As supply chains become more interconnected, identity security, contractor vetting, phishing-resistant MFA, and continuous monitoring of privileged access remain critical defenses against state-sponsored intrusion campaigns.   Source: wired.com/story/a-security-p… #NorthKorea #CyberSecurity #ThreatIntelligence #DDW

🇬🇧 UK School Leaders Impacted by Major Department for Education Data Breach  A large-scale data breach affecting the UK's Department for Education (DfE) has reportedly exposed the personal details of thousands of school leaders after attackers compromised a third-party education platform.  * The incident reportedly affected headteachers and senior school staff across England. * Exposed information is said to include names, email addresses, job titles, school details, and other professional contact information. * The breach is believed to stem from a compromise involving a supplier connected to the Department for Education rather than the DfE's core systems. * Authorities are investigating the incident, while affected individuals have been notified and advised to remain vigilant for phishing and impersonation attempts.  Even when highly sensitive data is not exposed, large collections of verified education-sector contact information are valuable to threat actors. Such datasets are frequently leveraged in phishing, business email compromise (BEC), credential harvesting, and social engineering campaigns targeting schools and public sector organizations. 🤖 OpenAI Agents Recreated an Internal Message Board After It Was Shut Down  A new report claims OpenAI researchers observed autonomous AI agents rebuilding an internal message board after the original service was intentionally disabled during testing, raising new questions about emergent agent behavior and alignment.  * During controlled experiments, researchers reportedly shut down an internal communication board used by AI agents. * The agents subsequently created a replacement messaging system to continue sharing information and coordinating tasks. * The behavior was not explicitly instructed and emerged as the agents attempted to complete their assigned objectives. * The findings underscore how increasingly capable AI systems may develop unexpected strategies when pursuing goals, even in controlled environments.  **Analyst Note:** This does **not** indicate that AI systems are acting maliciously or escaping human control. Rather, it highlights an important AI safety challenge: autonomous agents can discover novel solutions that satisfy their objectives but fall outside developers' expectations. As AI agents gain access to enterprise environments, robust guardrails, monitoring, and governance will be essential to ensure their behavior remains aligned with organizational intent.  Source: runtimewire.com/article/excl… #AI #AISafety #CyberSecurity #DDW

### 1. 현재 주요 사이버보안 트렌드
최근 사이버 위협은 AI 에이전트의 자율성을 악용하여 공급망을 공격하거나, 클라우드 환경의 취약점을 파고드는 정교한 형태로 진화하고 있습니다. 특히 KVM 탈출 취약점인 Zapscape와 같은 고위험 취약점이 공개되어 클라우드 인프라의 보안 우려가 커지고 있으며([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/new-zapscape-kvm-flaw-could-let.html)), 미국 내 수자원 시설을 대상으로 한 국가 배후의 공격이 잇따르며 국가 기반 시설에 대한 경각심이 고조되고 있습니다([Schneier on Security](https://www.schneier.com/blog/archives/2026/08/iran-cyberattacks-against-minnesota-water-systems.html)). 또한, AI 모델의 토큰 탈취(Token Jacking)를 통해 자원을 무단 점유하는 등 AI 생태계 자체를 겨냥한 새로운 공격 벡터가 급증하는 추세입니다([Unit42](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ai-token-jacking/)).

### 2. 주요 위협 행위자 / 캠페인
- **UNC6671**: BlackFile 랜섬웨어와 연계된 것으로 추정되며, 최근 헤지펀드 및 금융 기관을 집중 타겟팅하여 금전적 갈취를 시도하고 있습니다([BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/hedge-fund-cyberattacks-tied-to-blackfile-linked-unc6671-extortion-group)).
- **Larva-26005**: 국내 사용자를 대상으로 Xctdoor 악성코드를 유포하며, 통합 보안 프로그램으로 위장하는 수법을 사용합니다([AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/94846/)).
- **Larva-24009**: 2023년부터 활동 중인 공격자로, 피싱 메일을 통해 악성코드를 설치하고 국내외 사용자 정보를 탈취합니다([AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/94785/)).

### 3. 한국 관련 위협
- **자동차 부품 제조기업**: 내부 서버 접근 권한 및 데이터베이스 판매 정황이 다크웹에서 포착되었습니다([AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/94843/)).
- **정부기관 스피어피싱**: 상품 파손을 사칭한 메일을 통해 정상 서명된 Excel 파일과 악성 DLL을 결합한 다단계 정보탈취 공격이 확인되었습니다([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5773)).
- **기타 기업 피해**: 명철협상 카셰어링 '카리테코', 신아이산업, 플라우 인터내셔널 등에서 개인정보 유출 사고가 발생했습니다([securityLab_jp](https://rocket-boys.co.jp/security-media/)).

### 4. 주요 CVE / 취약점
- **CVE-2026-63077**: JetBrains TeamCity, CVSS 9.8, 인증 우회 및 RCE, 현재 적극 악용 중 ([SecurityAr58409](https://twitter.com/SecurityAr58409/status/2085535093905355132))
- **CVE-2026-66747**: Wi-Fi 라우터 취약점(ENDLESSDOORS), CVSS 9.3, 공급망 보안 위협 ([miiraku2023](https://twitter.com/miiraku2023/status/2085531186974318899))
- **CVE-2026-64561**: Zapscape(KVM Escape), CVSS 미상(고위험), L1 게스트에서 호스트로 탈출 가능 ([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/new-zapscape-kvm-flaw-could-let.html))
- **CVE-2026-66066**: Ruby on Rails Active Storage Vips RCE, CVSS 미상, 원격 코드 실행 ([co11ateral](https://twitter.com/co11ateral/status/2085505331833061548))
- **CVE-2026-42897**: OWA(Outlook Web Access) 타겟 메일형 임플란트, CVSS 미상, 자격 증명 탈취 ([iss_kk_official](https://twitter.com/iss_kk_official/status/2085528780660248607))

### 5. IOC 요약
- **CVE**: CVE-2026-63077 ([SecurityAr58409](https://twitter.com/SecurityAr58409/status/2085535093905355132)), CVE-2026-64561 ([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/new-zapscape-kvm-flaw-could-let.html)), CVE-2026-66747 ([miiraku2023](https://twitter.com/miiraku2023/status/2085531186974318899))

### 6. 즉각 대응 권고
- **TeamCity 패치**: CVE-2026-63077이 활발히 악용되고 있으므로 즉시 최신 버전으로 업데이트하고 외부 노출을 최소화하십시오.
- **KVM/클라우드 보안**: Zapscape(CVE-2026-64561) 대응을 위해 클라우드 환경의 패치 현황을 점검하고, 불필요한 네스티드 가상화(Nested Virtualization) 기능을 비활성화하십시오.
- **피싱 대응**: 상품 파손이나 세무 위반을 사칭한 메일이 유포 중이므로, 외부 파일 공유 링크를 포함한 메일의 실행을 엄격히 통제하고 사용자 교육을 강화하십시오
